setup: Lagrange's method: at a constrained optimum \(\nabla f = \lambda \nabla g\), here with \(f = xy\) and \(g = x + y - [[s]]\).

steps.say: Set up the conditions: \(f_x = \lambda g_x\) gives \(y = \lambda\), and \(f_y = \lambda g_y\) gives \(x = \lambda\).
So \(x = y\); the constraint \(x + y = [[s]]\) then gives \(x = y = [[s]]/2 = [[half]]\).
The product there is \([[half]] \cdot [[half]] = [[maximum]]\); a product with a fixed sum is largest when the factors are equal.
